findings.title: Async legacy writes use the (soon-to-be-cancelled) request context
findings.body: In Create (and identically in Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection), the legacy write is launched in a goroutine that derives its context from the incoming request `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)`. When Create returns to the caller, the API server completes the HTTP request and cancels the request context, which immediately cancels the goroutine's context as well. The 'safe measure' legacy write will therefore usually fail with context canceled before it even runs, so in mode 3 the legacy store will silently drift out of sync with unified storage. The goroutine should use a detached context (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`) while keeping only the values (logger, auth info) needed. This affects lines 51, 110, 135, and 163.

findings.title: Update passes the same UpdatedObjectInfo to both stores, losing the pre-computed updated object
findings.body: The previous implementation of mode 3 Update first did `Storage.Get`, called `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` once, and then wrapped the result in an `updateWrapper` so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update received a wrapper returning the already-computed object. The new code passes the raw `objInfo` to `d.Storage.Update` and then to `d.Legacy.Update` in the async goroutine. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` implementations used by the API machinery generally wrap the request body and may only be consumed once (e.g. they decode the incoming object on each call, or hold the old object fetched by the first Update call). The second invocation in the legacy goroutine can fail or produce an object computed against a different 'old' state than unified storage used, so legacy can store content that differs from what was written to unified storage — the opposite of what the dual write is meant to guarantee.

findings.title: Storage failures recorded with the legacy-duration metric
findings.body: In Create, when `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` — recording a legacy error/duration even though the legacy store was never called. The same mistake exists in Update at line 129 (`recordLegacyDuration` on a `d.Storage.Update` failure). This corrupts the dual-writer metrics: legacy error rates and latencies will show failures that actually belong to unified storage, misleading anyone alerting on these metrics during the migration.

findings.title: Delete records the object name as the metric 'kind' label
findings.body: On the success path of Delete, the metric is recorded as `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing the object name where every other call site passes `options.Kind`. This creates a high-cardinality metric label (one series per deleted object name) and breaks aggregation by kind for delete operations.

findings.title: DeleteCollection async legacy call recorded with the storage metric
findings.body: Inside the async goroutine of DeleteCollection, the result of `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will be attributed to unified storage, and the actual storage call was already recorded above, so every delete-collection produces two storage-metric samples and no legacy-metric sample.

findings.title: Delete installs the wrong logger into the context
findings.body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` with the base logger instead of `log`. All log lines emitted from within the storage/legacy delete calls (and the `log.Error` in this function uses `log`, but anything retrieved via klog.FromContext downstream) lose the name/kind/method values that the other methods attach.

findings.title: Tests don't verify the async legacy write happens
findings.body: The mode 3 write-path tests set up legacy mock expectations but then never wait for the goroutine or assert the legacy call occurred (e.g. TestMode3_Create's error case doesn't even set up a storage mock failing — the 'unified store fails' case configures only the legacy mock to fail, while the actual storage mock has no expectation, so `dw.Create` panics/fails on an unexpected call rather than exercising the intended path, and no test asserts `ls` was eventually called). As written, the tests pass even if the legacy write is dropped entirely (e.g. due to the cancelled-context bug), so they don't protect the core guarantee of mode 3.
